headline: Canadian Armed Forces Recruitment 2026: Eligibility, Tests and How to Apply
metaDescription: Canadian Armed Forces recruitment 2026: citizen or PR eligibility, age 17+, Grade 10 minimum, eCFAT test, FORCE fitness standards and application steps.

sections.content:
The basics for joining the Canadian Armed Forces are straightforward. You must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident and at least 17 years old — officer applicants can be 16 if they have been selected for a Royal Military College programme or civilian university entry. Anyone under 18 needs the consent of a parent or guardian on the day of enrolment.

On education, the floor is Grade 10 completed, or 24 credits of Secondary IV in Quebec, though many occupations demand more. If you finished school outside Canada, get your Educational Credential Assessment done for your high school and highest qualification before you apply — the recruiting system will not process the file without it.
sections.title: Eligibility: Citizenship, Age and Education

sections.content:
CAF selection runs as a six-stage process, and you must clear each stage to move to the next. It starts with the application form, personnel screening consent and two reference letters, then moves to the Canadian Forces Aptitude Test. A full medical examination follows — heart rate, blood pressure, cholesterol, vision, hearing and a urine sample are all covered.

Stage four is the fitness evaluation, stage five is the reliability check including a criminal record check, and the process closes with an interview with a military career counsellor assessing your personal qualities and motivation. It is competitive throughout: clearing every stage does not guarantee an offer of employment.
sections.title: The Six-Stage Selection Process

sections.content:
The eCFAT is the aptitude hurdle. It tests verbal skills with 15 questions in 5 minutes, spatial ability with 15 questions in 10 minutes, and problem solving with 30 questions in 30 minutes. It is designed to measure raw aptitude rather than what you studied in school, and your scores help determine which occupations you qualify for.

Because it is heavily time-pressured, the best preparation is practising timed reasoning questions until the format feels familiar. Speed matters as much as accuracy — many candidates know the material but lose marks to the clock. Arrive rested, read each question once, and keep moving.
sections.title: The Canadian Forces Aptitude Test

sections.content:
Physical readiness is measured by the FORCE Evaluation — Fitness for Operational Requirements of CAF Employment. It has four components: 20-metre rushes done as two shuttle sprints under 51 seconds, 30 consecutive lifts of a 20 kg sandbag to a metre above ground in under 3 minutes 30 seconds, 10 intermittent loaded shuttles alternating with and without a 20 kg sandbag in under 5 minutes 21 seconds, and dragging four 20 kg sandbags over 20 metres without stopping.

Train specifically for these events rather than general fitness. Sandbag work under time pressure is a skill — grip, lifting technique and pacing all matter. Candidates who rehearse the exact test format consistently outperform fitter candidates who walk in cold.
